newsitem.title: JAPAN: Toyota says not considering revising sales target.
newsitem.headline: Toyota says not considering revising sales target.

text.p: Toyota Motor Corp said on Monday that it was not considering revising its domestic sales target for calendar 1997.
"We are not considering revising the target," a Toyota spokesman said.
Toyota's current domestic sales target for 1997 is about 2.21 million units, up four percent from its actual domestic sales in 1996.

The Japanese business daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun said on Saturday that Toyota had told its dealers it was lowering its domestic sales target for calendar 1997 to 2.15 million vehicles, down 60,000 units from its original goal.
The paper said the carmaker had made the revision due to unexpectedly sluggish sales since April.
"We are planning to launch new models in the second half of this year and we will make efforts to meet the target," the Toyota spokesman said.

The spokesman said Toyota would also maintain its domestic production target of about 3.49 million units for 1997, its overseas production target of about 1.45 million units and its export target of about 1.33 million units.
